d.d: To cause to suffer; to trouble, afflict. (Now chiefly in interrogative or indefinite constructions.)
d.x: Have some chicken soup. It's good for what ails you.

d.d: To be ill; to suffer; to be troubled.
The awn of barley or other types of corn.
The hinged part on the trailing edge of an airplane wing, used to control longitudinal turns.
A half gable, as at the end of a penthouse or of the aisle of a church.
present participle and gerund of ail

d.x: She cared for her ailing brother day in, day out.
